newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN MAIZE BOARD SAYS NO EXPORT APPLICATIONS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN MAIZE BOARD SAYS NO EXPORT APPLICATIONS.

text.p: South Africa's Maize Board said on Thursday that no applications had been received for export permits for maize shipments during the months of February to April 1997.
"We received no applications," a board spokeswoman said.
Applications for export tenders closed on January 15. The spokeswoman said the next date for export permit applications would be February 14.
The country's Maize Advisory Committee recommended earlier this month that the deadline for application for export permits by private traders should be extended until April 30, 1997.
According to this season's maize marketing scheme private traders, who made their debut in the export market in the 1996/97 marketing year, may export up to 1.8 million tonnes of maize.

The Maize Board has said permits for exports totalling 1.66 million tonnes had already been issued. This comprised permits for 711,883 tonnes of white maize, 761,205 tonnes of yellow and 188,000 tonnes of maize products.
